title: Adaptive pinning and compatibility adapter for model/runtime pair routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement an "adaptive compatibility adapter" that centralizes decisions about model/runtime pinning and automatic fallbacks across version boundaries. The adapter will be a lightweight policy layer in the request routing path that consults a compatibility matrix, runtime health signals, and rollout gates to decide whether to route to a pinned model/runtime pair, a compatible variant, or a degraded tier.

Background: We currently support explicit version pins and a variety of fallback behaviors scattered across the router, model registry, and runtime. This has led to inconsistent behavior during staged upgrades: some tenants observe silent downgrades, others get 5xxs because the router attempted incompatible pairings, and rollback tooling is manual. We need a single source of truth with deterministic decision logic, richer telemetry, and testable rollout gates.

Goals:
- Provide deterministic routing decisions for pinned pairs and unpinned requests.
- Support multi-channel LTS semantics (stable, lts-1, experimental) and allow tenants to opt into channel upgrades.
- Automatic, observable fallbacks when runtime-model compatibility checks fail (graceful downgrade to a compatible quantized variant or to a fallback model family).
- Allow rollout gates: percentage canary, SLO/latency/regression thresholds, and automated pause/rollback.
- Minimal added latency to the critical path (target < 3ms median decision time).

Design overview: The compatibility adapter will expose a simple HTTP/gRPC API consumed by the router. Given a request (tenant, model id & desired version/channel, runtime pool attributes, request SLO target) it returns a routing decision: route_target (model_version_id or runtime_variant), decision_reason, probe_actions (optional), and a fallback plan (ordered list). The adapter will consult three inputs: the compatibility matrix (model-version -> runtime-ABI / kernel profile), dynamic runtime health metrics (node-level readiness, tail latency, memory pressure), and rollout policies (canary percent, metric thresholds).

Compatibility matrix and metadata: We'll extend model registry entries with attributes: supported_runtime_abis (list), min_runtime_version, recommended_quantization_profiles, and known_regressions (list of issue IDs). A compatibility probe will attempt a micro-inference (1-2 tokens) against candidate pairings during rollout windows to validate correctness.

Rollout gates: Support the following fences:
- Fractional canary: route X% of traffic deterministically (hashing by tenant)
- Telemetry gate: only proceed if no regression in top-k prompt evals and 95th percentile latency for the canary group below threshold
- Failure budget gate: if error rate for canary exceeds configured budget, automatically halt and select fallback

Fallback hierarchy (example):
1) Pinned model/runtime pair (if explicitly requested by tenant and compatible)
2) Same model, compatible runtime ABI or quantized variant
3) Compatible model in same family (recommended replacement)
4) Global lightweight fallback model (low-cost, best-effort)

Observability: The adapter will emit events for every non-trivial decision: decision_reason, matched_compatibility_rule, probe_results, canary cohort id, and resolution. Dashboards: canary health (latency, error rate), compatibility probe success rate, decision latency. We'll add tracing hooks to surface adapter decisions in request traces.

APIs and Backwards Compatibility: The routing API remains the same; the adapter adds a decision endpoint that returns a route target. Existing routers will be updated to call the adapter in a backward-compatible way: if the adapter is unavailable, router falls back to current heuristic with a warning. We will gate adapter adoption per-tenant before global enforcement.

Testing: Integration test harness will simulate version combinations with synthetic payloads and the real runtime in a staging pool. We'll add chaos tests that flip runtime ABI incompatibility flags to verify fallback paths. Canary experiments will run for 48 hours with traffic shaping in staging before production rollouts.

Migration path: Phase 1: Read-only adapter mode (no enforcement) with decision logging and dashboards. Phase 2: Opt-in enforcement for selected tenants. Phase 3: Default enforcement for new model registrations. Phase 4: Global enforcement and deprecation of legacy heuristics.

Open questions and trade-offs:
- How to encode behavioral compatibility (quality regressions) vs binary ABI incompatibility? Proposal: treat quality regressions as soft constraints enforced by telemetry gates rather than hard rejections.
- Storage and TTL for compatibility matrix entries (staleness risk). Proposal: TTL 90 days + model onboarding webhook to refresh.
- Can we reuse existing placement caches to avoid extra lookup latency? Likely yes; adapter will consult cache and subscribe to cache invalidation events.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter decision endpoint implemented with <5ms median latency in staging
Compatibility metadata schema extended in model registry and populated for top 25 models
Canary gate integration: percentage routing + telemetry gating + automatic halt/rollback
Failover chain invoked correctly in induced ABI incompatibility chaos tests
Decision logs emitted to events pipeline and surfaced in console dashboard
rollout_plan: Phase 0: implement adapter and run in read-only mode in staging (2 sprints). Phase 1: invite 3 pilot tenants, opt-in enforcement for traffic to their dedicated pools (1 sprint). Phase 2: expand to 25% of multi-tenant hosted pool traffic with canary gating (1 sprint). Phase 3: full enforcement and begin deprecating legacy heuristics (rolling, 2 sprints). Emergency rollback: route traffic back to pinned model version and mark adapter as read-only. All phases include 48h observation windows and predetermined SLO thresholds.
